_comment: Proposed changes to the printed digits, each graded I. Positions count symbols from 1 in transcription.txt. The printed digits stay as they are in transcription.txt.

repairs.why: dispositie: 14 (l) stands for t here and again in P522.1 at the same place in the same word; 27 is t everywhere else. A slip in the writer's or the decipherer's key for this word, or the printer's; the text needs t
gespeurt: printed 17 (n). u is also wanted in gequalificeert (P522.3); either u was written with the n-symbol or the print confuses 16 and 17 (16 is never printed)
'van ots verwac[ht]': ons is required; printed 27 (t) for 17 (n)
gequalificeert: printed 15 (m) for 5 (c); the 77 that follows is the ee symbol
propositie: '71' for '7.' with a stray 1; the next word, doen, is clean
the numeral fourteen left in clear inside the run: Birch glosses 'within [14 daghen]' as 'fourteen days'; as the l-symbol it gives no Dutch word
thien schepen: printed 27 (t) for 26 (s); Birch's gloss 'ten ships'
geloopen: '1' at the line end is 17 (n) with the 7 dropped; Birch's gloss 'were run away'
een cijffer (a cipher): printed 3 (a) where the ij symbol is needed; the context ('a character to open a lockt chest, I mean a cipher') is not in doubt

Splitting printed 43 into 4.3 gives ba under the existing alphabet and completes anabaptisten, agreeing with the English gloss. A dedicated ba group is an alternative; neither mechanism is established from this singleton. Do not add b or ba as a secure cryptanalytic key value.
